hexcasting.category.createmanaindustry.d: Bridging the gap between industrial $(thing)Create/$ machinery and $(hex)Hexcasting/$, automating the production of $(item)casting items/$, $(item)media batteries/$, and more.
hexcasting.page.createmanaindustry.casti: Crafting $(thing)casting items/$ has always been tedious, and never without a hexer's hand in it — far too slow for my liking. So I built a $(thing)sequenced assembly line/$: a $(thing)Deployer/$, a $(thing)Spout/$, and a $(thing)Mechanical Press/$ in three steps, turning out items indistinguishable from handiwork.

$(bold)Step One: Scribe/$ — a $(thing)Deployer/$ aims at a fresh casting item on a $(thing)Depot/$ and copies a pattern from an $(item)Iota-bearing item/$ — a $(item)Scroll/$, $(item)Spellbook/$, $(item)Abacus/$, $(item)Slate/$, or $(item)Focus/$ — yielding an $(thing)incomplete/$ variant. Run it again to inscribe further Iota.$(br2)The held item is never consumed.

$(bold)Step Two: Fill/$ — a $(thing)Spout/$ pumps $(media)Liquid Media/$ into the piece. Capacity by tier:$(br)$(li)$(item)Cypher/$ — $(item)640 Amethyst Dust/$$(br)$(li)$(item)Trinket/$ — $(item)7,680 Amethyst Dust/$$(br)$(li)$(item)Artifact/$ — $(item)92,160 Amethyst Dust/$$(br2)Each pour adds up to a bucket; fill in passes. Capacities are configurable.

$(bold)Step Three: Press/$ — a $(thing)Mechanical Press/$ stamps the inscribed, filled piece into a finished item, carrying over every $(thing)Iota/$, $(thing)pattern/$, drop of Media, and $(item)dye/$ — a complete casting item, ready for spellwork.
hexcasting.page.createmanaindustry.indus: The times move on, and so does technique. Knowing Hex Casting well enough by now, I joined its lore to the ways of machinery — and from that union came these industrial patterns, and an industrialized craft of Media. Magic was never mysterious; Hex Casting is merely a craft lost for too long. I am good with it, and upon it I will build my glory.

Industrial patterns need not be drawn by hand alone — this mod registers $(thing)Stonecutting/$ recipes dynamically at startup, stamping any Hexcasting pattern save for Great Spells straight onto a $(item)Blank Slate/$. The recipes mirror the installed pattern registry exactly — addons' patterns included.

To use it:$(br)$(li)place a $(item)Blank Slate/$ in a $(thing)Stonecutter/$$(br)$(li)scroll the list — recipes are grouped by mod namespace$(br)$(li)pick a pattern to get a $(thing)pre-patterned Slate/$$(br2)It transcribes like any other Slate through standard $(thing)Pattern Transcription/$.
$(thing)Great Spells/$ cannot be cut — not even when I know their drawing.

Light a $(item)Blaze Burner/$ or $(item)Allay Burner/$ from afar. Consumes a $(thing)vector/$ (the position) and a $(thing)number/$ (seconds of burn) to add exactly that much burn time.$(br2)Media is charged per second at the burner's own burn rate, making this exactly as economical as pouring in $(media)Liquid Media/$. Burners without a Blaze inside cannot be lit; invalid targets end in a $(thing)miscast/$.

Read the $(thing)Iota/$ stored on an item resting on a $(item)Depot/$ or $(item)Placard/$ straight off the block, pushing it onto the $(thing)stack/$ — no need to pick the item up.$(br2)Consumes one $(thing)vector/$ — the position. Miscasts if the target is not a Depot or Placard, holds no item, or the item bears no Iota.

So this is what they call $(thing)Enlightenment/$ — a wondrous, strange feeling. A $(thing)Great Work/$... now that is a fine design. And now I see what Slates are for... $(thing)Spell Circles/$? A fine thing indeed. Should the chance arise, I will set one among my newest machines — for I have seen enough. I will build the Great Work anew; I am destiny's own.

A spell circle is itself a machine: a lattice of $(item)Slates/$ that, once activated, executes whatever pattern is inscribed upon it. And here it meets industry — a census of those who enter, ready to feed the $(l:createmanaindustry/casting_item_production)$(thing)production line/$.$(br2)Circle patterns are worked through the $(l:createmanaindustry/industrial_patterns)$(thing)Stonecutting/$ — stamp them on Slates and let the circle run.

Take a census of a spell circle: it inspects the circle's own bounds — the region told of by $(thing)Lesser Fold Reflection/$ and $(thing)Greater Fold Reflection/$ — and pushes a $(thing)list/$ of the $(thing)entities/$ of every $(thing)player/$ standing within.$(br2)The dead are not counted, and order is not guaranteed. Cast outside a circle — via a $(thing)casting item/$, say — and it $(thing)miscasts/$.
hexcasting.page.createmanaindustry.media: Wielding Media in its crystalline form is a wasteful business — the liquid Media stored within casting items suffers no such loss. In ages past, a hexer could barely draw Media out of amethyst without the aid of spellcraft; with today's machinery, it is simply pressed out.

A finished $(item)Phial of Media/$ exchanges $(media)Liquid Media/$ directly with Create's $(thing)fluid network/$. Set the phial on a $(thing)Depot/$ above a $(item)Drain/$: the drain siphons it out for transport by $(thing)Fluid Pipes/$ or storage in tanks, while a $(thing)Spout/$ pumps Liquid Media back in.$(br2)Phials make ideal $(thing)Media buffers/$ in automated hexing: release when scarce, refill when plentiful.

One bucket of Liquid Media holds the equivalent of $(item)40 Amethyst Dust/$, and a full phial holds $(thing)92,160 Dust/$ — roughly $(thing)2,304 buckets/$.$(br2)Do the math, and your line can juggle plenty and dearth with ease.

$(media)Liquid Media/$ is the heart of the whole line: amethyst pressed into liquid, stored in $(item)Phials of Media/$, poured into $(item)casting items/$ for spellwork, and fed to $(item)burners/$ as fuel.$(br2)One fluid, threading through the $(l:createmanaindustry/casting_item_production)$(thing)Casting Item Line/$ and the $(l:createmanaindustry/industrial_patterns)$(thing)Industrial Patterns/$ alike — the seed of an industrial Media economy.

$(media)Liquid Media/$ is a $(thing)Create fluid/$ — raw Hexcasting Media condensed into a form that flows through $(thing)Fluid Pipes/$. It glows with a soft pink light, easy to spot in tanks and basins.

$(thing)Heated Compaction/$ converts amethyst materials directly into $(media)Liquid Media/$:$(br)$(li)$(item)Amethyst Dust/$ — 25 mB$(br)$(li)$(item)Amethyst Shard/$ — 125 mB$(br)$(li)$(item)Charged Amethyst/$ — 250 mB$(br2)Compaction requires $(thing)heat/$; an ordinary $(item)Blaze Burner/$ suffices.

$(media)Liquid Media/$ can be worked further:$(br)$(li)$(thing)Heated Mixing/$ turns it into $(item)Liquid Mana/$ at a 1:1 ratio.$(br)$(li)In a $(item)Kinetic Atomizer/$, that Mana is $(thing)mixed/$ into a mist of $(media)Liquid Media/$ vapour.$(br)$(li)A $(item)Condenser/$ set in the mist gathers it back into usable $(media)Liquid Media/$, closing the loop.$(br2)Mana flows between liquid forms as readily as you please.

Converting amethyst into $(media)Liquid Media/$:$(br)$(li)1 $(item)Amethyst Dust/$ — 25 mB$(br)$(li)1 $(item)Amethyst Shard/$ — 125 mB$(br)$(li)1 $(item)Charged Amethyst/$ — 250 mB$(br2)Outputs scale with the server's $(thing)mediaPerBucket/$ and Hexcasting's own $(thing)Media numbers/$.

The $(item)Phials of Media/$ that hold liquid Media seem to be of a peculiar nature — they can only be made through the art of $(thing)Make Phial/$. That is a craft lost to time; to work it, I must hunt down $(item)Ancient Scrolls/$ left in some forgotten corner.

Modern machinery suffices: hand an $(item)Ancient Scroll/$ carved with the $(thing)Make Phial/$ pattern to a $(thing)Deployer/$ facing a $(item)Glass Bottle/$ on a $(thing)Depot/$, and you will have an $(thing)incomplete Media Phial/$.$(br2)The scroll must bear the right pattern, or the craft fails.

Fill the incomplete phial with $(media)Liquid Media/$ through a $(thing)Spout/$, then $(thing)press/$ it under a $(item)Mechanical Press/$ — the result is a finished $(item)Phial of Media/$ holding the equivalent of $(item)92,160 Amethyst Dust/$.$(br2)A phial's capacity equals the Media you pour in: you decide how much power it stores.
hexcasting.page.createmanaindustry.trick: The Tricksters keep spells in knots, a path as intricate as Hex Casting though far apart from it. If I can harness their $(thing)spells/$, my line will want for nothing.$(br2)These pages describe reading a Trickster spell from your held item, casting it with $(thing)Hermes' Gambit/$, and converting Media into mana stored in carried knots.

$(thing)Hermes' Gambit/$ can run a $(thing)Trick Iota/$ in the Trickster execution environment. With arguments, place a $(thing)list/$ below the Trick Iota: $(thing)list, trick, Hermes/$; without arguments, use $(thing)trick, Hermes/$. A Trick Iota also runs when encountered unescaped in an evaluated Hex list, consuming an optional argument list from the top of the stack.$(br2)Spells that finish in the same tick push their result back onto the $(thing)stack/$; longer ones continue across ticks in the background and return nothing. Failed spells log an error and push no result; the spell and any argument list are still consumed.$(br2)Trickster spells spend $(thing)mana/$ from the player's carried knots or a $(item)Spell Construct/$'s inventory. In a $(thing)spell circle/$, they draw mana from knots embedded in reached $(item)Slates/$, even without a player. The source position is the executing slate or construct. Hexcasting $(thing)media/$ remains separate.$(br2)Unbound block sources can run up to five background spells; unloading or restarting cancels those temporary jobs. A bound circle keeps the calling slate's position, direction and world, while I provide my identity and items, even from another dimension. Its saved jobs pause while I am offline or a source chunk is unloaded, and resume when the same sources return. Replacing a source ends its jobs; changing a knot uses the new knot's current balance. I can cancel a waiting job through Trickster's spell slots. Cross-language calls share instruction limits and a default nesting limit of 32. Tricks that require a player still require one.

Read a $(thing)Trickster spell/$ from the spell item held in your other hand, pushing the whole $(thing)spell tree/$ onto the stack as a $(thing)Trick Iota/$.$(br2)Costs no Media — pure reading. If no spell-bearing item is held, it $(thing)miscasts/$ and the stack is untouched.

A $(thing)Trick Iota/$ is a Hexcasting Iota carrying a complete $(thing)Trickster/$ spell — an entire $(thing)spell tree/$ — just like any other Iota: storable in $(item)Scrolls/$ and $(item)Slates/$, writable into casting items by a $(l:createmanaindustry/casting_item_production)$(thing)Deployer/$, able to travel the stack.$(br2)Its contents render through the $(thing)Inline/$ library, so spell trees show fully in Iota displays and the like. $(l:createmanaindustry/trickster_patterns#createmanaindustry:read_trick_from_item)$(thing)Unknotting/$ creates it and $(l:createmanaindustry/trickster_patterns#trick_eval)$(thing)Hermes' Gambit/$ runs it. Consideration and parentheses keep it as data when needed.
hexcasting.page.createmanaindustry.ysm_m: Great Spell. Inputs, in order: the target player and that player's complete root-group list. Temporarily applies the model to the player. The default cost is one Charged Amethyst's worth of Media; the server can change it. The temporary change ends when you cast Restore, the player leaves the server, or the player changes models manually.
Takes no inputs. Creates a default cube. Use property indexes 0 and 1 to set its origin and size, and 7 to set its face UVs; then add it to a group's cube list (property index 9). Costs no Media.

Takes no inputs. Creates an empty group named “bone”. Use property index 8 to name it, 9 to give it cubes, and 10 to give it child groups. Add the new group to a group in your model before applying or exporting; it costs no Media.

Cube property indexes (origin, size, and pivot use model pixels; rotations use degrees; scale is a factor; UV coordinates and sizes use texture pixels):$(br)$(li)0 Origin: vector$(br)$(li)1 Size: vector$(br)$(li)2 Pivot: vector$(br)$(li)3 Rotation: vector$(br)$(li)4 Scale: vector$(br)$(li)5 Inflate: number$(br)$(li)6 Visible: boolean$(br)$(li)7 UV: a list of six faces in north, south, east, west, up, down order; each face is [u, v, width, height, rotation, visible]. Rotation can be 0, 90, 180, or 270.

Example: add a cube to an existing bone. Follow child groups with index 10, using index 8 to check their names; read the bone's cube list with index 9. Create a cube, set its origin and size, add it to the list, and write the list back with index 9. If the bone has a parent, put the edited bone into that parent's child list with index 10. Continue up to the root, then replace that root in the original full list. Keep the parts you did not edit.

Great Spell. Input: the complete root-group list of one model. Exports a copy to the caster's client under exports/. This does not change a player's current model, and the caster must be connected to the game. The default cost is one Charged Amethyst's worth of Media; the server can change it.

Arguments, in order: a group or cube, then a property index. The index must be a whole number from 0 to 13. The pattern returns that property's value. Check the tables below and choose a property available on that object. Costs no Media.

Group property indexes (pivot uses model pixels; rotation uses degrees; scale is a factor):$(br)$(li)2 Pivot: vector$(br)$(li)3 Rotation: vector$(br)$(li)4 Scale: vector$(br)$(li)6 Visible: boolean$(br)$(li)8 Name: string$(br)$(li)9 Cubes: list of cubes$(br)$(li)10 Children: list of groups$(br)$(li)11 Texture size: vector, top-level groups only, in [positive width, positive height, 0] form$(br)$(li)12 Part label and 13 Source label: strings that can only be read. Other indexes do not apply to groups.

With YSM installed, Hex Casting can read and edit player models. A model is made of $(thing)groups/$ and the $(thing)cubes/$ inside them: groups follow the bones, while cubes make up the visible shape. Usually, read a player's model, follow its child groups to the part you want, edit its properties, and write each change back up the tree before applying the whole model.$(br2)For Read, Apply, and Restore, the target player must be in range and in the same dimension. Scrolls, Slates, and other items carrying model data belong with their world save.

Apply and Export need the complete root-group list you got when reading one model. Do not remove untouched parts or combine roots from different models. Add new groups and cubes to the model you read before applying or exporting them.

Give Read Player Model a target player. It pushes a list of the top-level groups in the player's selected model onto the $(thing)stack/$. Keep the whole list; Apply and Export need it later. The target must be in range, in the same dimension, and have a YSM model that can be read. If the model is not ready yet, try again in a moment. This Great Spell costs no Media.

Input: the target player. Restores the model they had before the temporary change. Costs no Media. The target must be in range and in the same dimension; leaving the server also restores the previous model.

Arguments, in order: a group or cube, a property index, then a value. Use the value type shown in the tables; lists must contain the matching kind of item. The pattern returns the edited group or cube. Properties that do not apply, and read-only indexes 12 and 13, cannot be set. To include the change in your model, put the result back in its list and write it back up to the top-level group. Costs no Media.
createmanaindustry.bnb_chain.no_core: This Modular Spell Construct has no kinetics core to link
createmanaindustry.partition.infinite_co: The target is in another partition. Its infinite distance cannot be paid.
createmanaindustry.partition.restore_fai: Partition could not be restored: its boundary conflicts with another partition or its coordinates are no longer valid. The spell continues.
createmanaindustry.configuration.partiti: Maximum GPU samples for Partition edges and membranes. Reducing or disabling visuals does not remove barriers.
An Allay Burner needs an Allay and a supply of fuel.
Hold an empty burner and right-click an Allay to capture it.
The filled burner is now ready to place in your workstation.
Capturing an Allay does not light the burner. Feed it first.
An Amethyst Shard starts the fire. You can now use its heat.
createmanaindustry.ponder.allay_fuel.tex: Feed the Allay Burner with Amethyst Shards to provide heat.
More fuel adds more burning time. It does not create a hotter tier.
Allay Burners are Mechanical Arm targets. A configured arm can feed them Amethyst Shards.
Keep shards on the Depot and the arm can replenish the burner.
createmanaindustry.ponder.allay_liquid.t: A bucket of Liquid Media can also fuel the burner.
The internal tank holds one bucket. Pipes can insert Liquid Media, but cannot extract it.
Solid fuel is used first. Liquid Media waits until that fuel runs out.
Keep the supply topped up for unattended heating.
createmanaindustry.ponder.allay_heat_lev: An empty burner has no Allay and supplies no processing heat.
Without fuel, an Allay Burner cannot provide heat for processing.
Both fuel types provide Allay Heat. When the fuel runs out, the burner stops providing heat.
Allay Heat covers ordinary Heated recipes: mix 250 mB of Liquid Media into 125 mB of Liquid Mana.
It also covers Superheated recipes: one Rose Quartz melts into 250 mB of molten liquid.
Allay Heat is the next tier above Superheated. A superheated Blaze Burner cannot vaporize this liquid.
A burning Allay Burner vaporizes the 125 mB. Its Allay Heat covers Heated, Superheated and Allay-heated recipes.
Heated compacting turns Amethyst Shards into Liquid Media.
The shard in the Basin is the ingredient; the burner below needs its own fuel.
The press turns the shard into Liquid Media. Its yield follows the server configuration.
Pump the result into storage or another machine.
createmanaindustry.ponder.allay_music.te: The Allay Burner also works as a jukebox.
Right-click with a music disc to insert it, just like a jukebox.
A music disc is not fuel. Music alone does not heat a Basin.
You can feed the burner while the disc is inside.
Right-click with an empty hand to take the disc out again.
Driving a spell core with a chain
Install a Kinetics Spell Core in a Modular Spell Construct.
This connection uses the cogwheel chains provided by Bits 'n' Bobs.
Link the powered cogwheel to the core with a chain. Nearby rotation alone is not a connection.
While the connected chain turns, the core can execute its spell. More speed raises its execution allowance.
Stop the chain and this core's execution allowance becomes zero. Restore rotation to resume.
createmanaindustry.ponder.hex_spells.tex: A Focus in the Deployer supplies the stored pattern to write into a spell item.
Each application appends its stored Iota. The Focus is kept, so you can use it again.
Fill the unfinished item with Liquid Media. Repeated filling increases its stored media up to its limit.
The press finishes the item while retaining its written patterns, media and pigment.
Trinkets and Artifacts follow the same steps. Finished Cyphers are single-use and cannot be refilled.
createmanaindustry.ponder.hex_battery.te: Apply the battery-crafting scroll to a Glass Bottle. Other patterns fail; the correct scroll is kept.
Fill with Liquid Media before pressing. You may repeat filling to store more media.
The press creates a finished Media Battery containing the media you supplied.
Its final capacity is set by how much media was filled before pressing.
createmanaindustry.ponder.hex_battery_tr: A finished Media Battery can exchange its stored media as Liquid Media.
Use an Item Drain to empty it. The bottle remains; its stored media decreases.
A Spout fills the same bottle again with Liquid Media.
Refilling restores its contents but does not increase the capacity set during crafting.
createmanaindustry.ponder.atomizer_setup: An Atomizer turns supplied liquid into a mist field while rotating.
Feed the back of the nozzle. An upward-facing atomizer takes liquid from below.
Mesh a cogwheel with its cog. A pipe alone does not provide rotation.
The mist has the same fluid type as the liquid you supply.
Molten fluids cannot enter this machine. Make their mist with a vaporizing recipe instead.
createmanaindustry.ponder.atomizer_range: Start with a slow atomizer and keep the machine you want to supply nearby.
More speed spreads the mist farther and uses liquid faster.
Mist is thinner farther from its source. Put demanding recipes closer to the atomizer.
An empty tank stops mist production even if the cog is still turning.
No rotation means no mist either. Check both power and fluid supply.
createmanaindustry.ponder.water_mist_irr: Supply a Kinetic Atomizer with water and rotational force to produce water mist
The water mist concentration at the farmland must be greater than 10%%
This keeps the farmland hydrated without a nearby water source
Mist becomes thinner farther from its source
Increasing the rotation speed allows the mist to reach more distant farmland
Once the mist disperses, the farmland will gradually dry out
A burning Allay Burner produces Liquid Soul mist around itself.
Place a Condenser inside the mist, with an Item Drain directly below it.
Pump Coolant through the condenser. Ordinary water does not work.
Cooling consumes Coolant and mist. Liquid Soul collects in the drain below.
Use a separate pipe to move the collected soul liquid into storage.
createmanaindustry.ponder.condenser_setu: Run Coolant along the condenser's pipe axis, with somewhere for the remaining coolant to go.
The product drops into an Item Drain below; it does not leave through the coolant pipe.
Without the drain directly underneath, nothing can be collected.
A full drain, or one holding a different liquid, also stops collection.
Pump out the product to keep working. Oxidized and waxed condensers work the same way.
A Mana Cogwheel generates rotation inside Liquid Mana mist.
This rotation can drive Create machines, such as this Millstone. Keep the total load within the cogwheel's stress capacity.
Liquid Media mist reverses that direction. Plan the connected machines accordingly.
Andesite and Brass Casings can enclose a Mana Cogwheel without changing its mist-powered operation.
Sneak and right-click with a wrench to remove either casing.
The mist must reach the cogwheel, even when encased. Losing the mist stops its generated rotation.
createmanaindustry.ponder.media_conversi: Converting Liquid Media into Liquid Mana requires Heated mixing.
Each batch consumes 250 mB of Liquid Media.
Mixing produces 125 mB of Liquid Mana: half the input volume.
Store it for mana-based machines and item filling.
This recipe needs Allay Heat and Liquid Media mist at the same time.
Supply Media mist with an atomizer. The burner's own Soul mist is a different fluid.
Add 32 Glass and one Iron Nugget to the Basin.
With both requirements met, mixing produces eight Amethyst Blocks.
Keep the Basin close enough to the atomizer for the mist to be concentrated enough.
createmanaindustry.ponder.amethyst_depos: Put an Iron Sheet into a Basin to make an amethyst-coated sheet.
Place a Framed Glass Trapdoor in the lower half of the block directly above the Basin.
Surround the Basin with Liquid Media mist. This coating does not need a heater.
Close the lid to begin deposition. Opening it interrupts the process.
The coated sheet is ready. Copper, gold and brass sheets use the same method.
createmanaindustry.ponder.rose_depositio: Start with Molten Rose Quartz in a Basin above a lit Allay Burner, with its Framed Glass Trapdoor open.
Vaporizing turns the molten liquid into mist. An Atomizer cannot do this job.
Place an Iron Sheet in a second Basin inside the mist, with heat underneath.
Close its Framed Glass Trapdoor. Heat and rose quartz mist produce the coating.
The same process coats copper, gold and brass sheets. Keep supplying the vaporizing Basin.
createmanaindustry.ponder.rose_quartz.te: Rose Quartz melts by Superheated compacting. Allay Heat also meets this requirement.
One Rose Quartz becomes 250 mB of molten liquid.
Replace the press with an open Framed Glass Trapdoor to vaporize it using Allay Heat.
Each operation vaporizes 125 mB. Use this mist for rose quartz deposition nearby.
createmanaindustry.ponder.coolant.text_1: Coolant is the liquid consumed by Condensers when they collect mist.
createmanaindustry.ponder.coolant.text_2: Compacting one block of Ice makes Coolant without any heating requirement.
createmanaindustry.ponder.coolant.text_3: One Ice becomes one bucket of Coolant.
createmanaindustry.ponder.coolant.text_4: Store the result and pump it through your cooling circuit.
Sweet Berries and water can be mixed into Liquid Source.
Each batch mixes one Sweet Berry with 25 mB of water; no heat is needed.
The finished batch contains 25 mB of Liquid Source.
A berry farm and a steady water supply can keep this simple production line running.
createmanaindustry.ponder.trickster_knot: Begin with an Emerald on the belt and Glass in the Deployer's hand.
The Deployer makes an incomplete Emerald Knot, ready for mana infusion.
Repeat Liquid Mana filling until its creation cost is met. Filling itself completes the knot.
Stop here for an intact knot. The press is an optional next step: it cracks the knot.
The output is a Cracked Emerald Knot. Other knot types have their own ingredients and mana costs.
createmanaindustry.ponder.trickster_char: The Kinetic Mana Generator consumes rotational stress to charge nearby knot storage.
Put a Charging Array directly on its output face. Here, the output points upwards.
Mechanical Arms can deliver knots to Charging Arrays and Spell Constructs.
Arrays expose their knot slots; Spell Constructs expose only the first slot and can also receive power on this face.
Adjust the scroll control to spend more stress per RPM. Make sure your power source can carry the load.
Charging stops without rotation or when the network is overstressed.
createmanaindustry.ponder.trickster_disp: A Display Link can send an inventory's item count to a Spell Construct.
Link the inventory to the construct, then choose the item-count source and destination argument slot.
The first argument now receives 32. Your spell can read this argument to react to the stock level.
Updated counts replace the argument. On a Modular Spell Construct, also choose the intended executor.
createmanaindustry.ponder.tag.processing: Heat, coat and process materials with Create machinery
createmanaindustry.ponder.tag.mist.descr: Make mist, collect it and use it to power machines
createmanaindustry.ponder.tag.magic_auto: Charge, assemble and connect magical items
createmanaindustry.configuration.allaySt: Local Storm particles, distant members and shader-pack shadow quality. Does not change combat.
createmanaindustry.configuration.package: Local package GPU geometry capture budget and collision capacity.
Client frame allowance shared by geometry capture and atlas upload, in milliseconds. Capture reserves half for upload; force/world reads and solver submission are measured separately.
Maximum resident GPU package collision sections for this client, clamped to the device SSBO limit. Light capacity is separate; changes apply on re-entering the world.
createmanaindustry.configuration.gridSna: Fraction of one grid spacing to travel before snapping to the next dot; the capture radius is (1 - value) times the spacing.
createmanaindustry.configuration.shaderP: FULL uses Iris casting. COARSE can skip the Storm body. RT uses qualified light occlusion. OFF disables MODEL shadow casting.
createmanaindustry.configuration.simulat: AUTO prefers OptiX, then DXR, and falls back to OpenGL on failure. Explicit DXR and OptiX retain the last frame on failure.
GPU for native Storm simulation. OpenGL uses Minecraft's GPU. Changes apply after the current Storm ends.
Pin this GPU. Supports %s. PCI address %s.
createmanaindustry.configuration.allayFe: Target total feathers per second over the whole 2R field at storm radius 32, scaled by (R/32)^2. Spawn points are sampled uniformly across the 2R disk and accepted with weight 1 inside R and (2R - d)/R out to 2R, so density falls off linearly from R to 2R. 0 stops new feathers; existing ones finish their lifetime.
createmanaindustry.configuration.allayGo: Target total gold particles per second over the whole 2R field at storm radius 32, scaled by (R/32)^2. Uses the same radial weight as feathers. 0 stops new particles.
createmanaindustry.configuration.stormLo: Distance in blocks where distant body geometry changes to billboards.
Display/subscription distance in blocks, capped by the server's stormLodMaxDistance. 0 disables distant members.
createmanaindustry.configuration.sameFat: Maximum ribbon, star and dissolution records within the shared GPU pool.
createmanaindustry.configuration.riftSky: Clip target sky; lighting and history may differ.
createmanaindustry.configuration.riftCul: Skip hidden portal visuals. Combat continues; unavailable depth falls back to frustum.
